procedural_matters: The arbitrator decided that RRS 44.1(b) may apply and the arbitration meeting will not be held.
The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
GER 3450 was represented by Julia Ewald.
GBR 3606 was represented by Lila Edwards.
GER 3450 presented photo evidence of the damage.
facts: The incident occurred in race F2 of the Silver fleet, on leg 1 and the wind speed was 18 to 25 knots and very gusty.
GER 3450 and GBR 3606 rounded mark 1, both on starboard tack, with GER 3450 overlapped to windward of GBR 3606 at a distance of 3 metres.
After rounding the mark, both boats bore away to a reaching course and they were in the process of hoisting their gennakers.
Both boats held their courses and maintained the distance between the hulls.
GER 3450 accelerated in a gust and heeled to leeward.
As GBR 3606 was blanketed by GER 3450, she heeled rapidly to windward.
There was a contact between the masthead of GBR 3606 and the mainsail of GER 3450, resulting in a 20 cm hole in the upper part of GER 3450's mainsail.
conclusions: GER 3450, the windward boat, failed to keep clear of GBR 3606, the leeward boat, and broke RRS 11.

It was reasonable possible for GER 3450, as the boat required to keep clear, to avoid contact by keeping a greater distance between the boats, considering the prevailing conditions. Therefore, she broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonable possible for GBR 3606, the right-of-way boat, to avoid contact when it became clear that GER 3450 is not keeping clear. Therefore, she did not break RRS 14(a).
decision: GER 3450 is scored DSQ in race F2.
